title: Remove the bracket breakdown module
description:
The bracket breakdown command module has no production caller. Removing it, with the code and prose that exist only for it, shrinks the command layer by about 550 lines.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/commands/breakdown.rs` (547 lines) is a private module (`commands/mod.rs:31`) re-exported as `BracketBreakdownResult` and `BracketChild` (`commands/mod.rs:74`). No production code calls `bracket_breakdown` or `bracket_breakdown_with_template`. The module opens one mutation session per child (`breakdown.rs:406`) and one per edge (`breakdown.rs:424,433,450`).

Its consumers are tests and prose:

- `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/bracket_breakdown_tests.rs` (the whole file, declared at `fast_docs_templates/main.rs:15`).
- The breakdown halves of two tests in `fast_docs_templates/template_binding_tests.rs:162-175,207-220,272-278`, with its module doc at `:13-21`.
- A doctest at `breakdown.rs:32-56`.
- Module docs in `tests/cli_repo_workflow/template_binding_cli_tests.rs:18-20` and `tests/cli_gate/bracket_coverage_gate_run_test.rs:16-18,151`.

`CommandExecutor::template_roles` (`commands/template.rs:103`) has one caller, `breakdown.rs:327`. Its doc comment (`template.rs:97-101`) lists breakdown as a consumer.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `commands/breakdown.rs`, its module declaration and its re-exports no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: `CommandExecutor::template_roles` no longer exists, and no doc comment lists breakdown as a template-role consumer.
- [hard] REQ-03: No test, doctest or test-module doc comment names `bracket_breakdown`, `BracketChild` or `BracketBreakdownResult`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The template-binding tests keep their template-apply and forced-refresh assertions.

## Notes

Nothing in production consumes breakdown, so its tests are deleted, not rewritten. No test asserting the module's absence is added.

planning.outcome: The bracket breakdown module, its orphaned template-role helper, and its tests are gone.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One module deletion with its test file and four prose sites.

title: Remove the silent integrity validator
description:
`validate_integrity_silent` and its three private helpers have no caller and re-implement integrity checks that repository validation already owns. One of them reaches git through libgit2 and resolves paths against the process working directory.

## Background

`validate_integrity_silent` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1835-1916`) has no caller. Its private helpers have no other caller:

- `validate_document_references` (`validate.rs:2466-2545`).
- `check_file_exists_in_git` (`validate.rs:2547-2561`).
- `validate_transitive_reduction` (`validate.rs:2590-2638`).

Together they span about 245 lines. They duplicate the document, DAG and transitive-reduction checks in `validation/repository.rs:457-503` and the claims-index check at `:550`.

`validate_document_references` opens a git2 repository on the selected worktree (`validate.rs:2470-2471`). Its working-tree fallback `Path::new(&doc.path).exists()` (`validate.rs:2521,2532`) resolves a repo-relative path against the process working directory. These helpers hold the file's only git2 use.

`validate_claims_index_with_paths` stays, because `validate_claims_index_at` (`validate.rs:3045`) also calls it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `validate_integrity_silent`, `validate_document_references`, `check_file_exists_in_git` and `validate_transitive_reduction` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: `commands/validate.rs` contains no `git2` use.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repository validation's document, DAG, transitive-reduction and claims-index checks keep their existing tests and behaviour.

## Notes

Deletion only. No test asserting the functions' absence is added.

planning.outcome: The uncalled silent integrity validator, with its libgit2 document-reference check, is gone.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Four uncalled functions in one file, removed with no rewrite target.

title: Keep one enforcement drift function
description:
Enforcement drift has a strict function that only its own tests call, beside the tolerant function production uses. One function remains, under the plain name.

## Background

`drift::enforcement_drift` (`crates/jit/src/validation/drift.rs:107`) has 11 callers, all of them tests in `drift.rs:252-376`. Production calls `enforcement_drift_tolerant` at `commands/validate.rs:1743,1777` and `validation/repository.rs:613,618`. The `_tolerant` suffix exists only to tell it apart from the strict twin. Its rustdoc says its semantics "extend [`enforcement_drift`]" (`drift.rs:149`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The test-only strict function no longer exists, and the surviving function is named `enforcement_drift`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No identifier, call site or doctest names `enforcement_drift_tolerant`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The drift tests exercise the surviving function with loaded rule and gate sources (`SourceState::Loaded`), covering the cases the strict-function tests covered.
- [hard] REQ-04: The surviving function's rustdoc states its own semantics and refers to no removed function.

## Notes

The tests stay in the pure validation layer.

planning.outcome: Enforcement drift has one function, named enforcement_drift, which production and tests both call.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One function removal, a four-site rename, and eleven test rewrites.

title: Remove linked-worktree evidence from repository capture
description:
Repository capture records linked-worktree evidence that only tests request. Every JSON capture still resolves worktree paths for it, and that resolution can spawn git.

## Background

Only tests request linked-worktree evidence: `CaptureSpec::discover_linked_worktree` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:719`) is called from `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:160` and `image.rs:1746`. Even so, `capture_over` calls `configured_worktree_paths()` on every JSON capture (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:597`). The value is threaded into `capture_capability_image` (`:1108`) and then `capture_linked_evidence` (`:1583`), its only use. `JsonFileStorage::configured_worktree_paths` (`storage/json.rs:560`) reaches `WorktreePaths::detect_for_data_root`, which runs `git` (`worktree_paths.rs:64`).

The evidence spans these sites:

- Capture spec: `CaptureSpec.linked_worktree` (`image.rs:630,645`), `discover_linked_worktree` (`:719-722`), `linked_worktree()` (`:752`).
- Image: `RepositoryImage.linked_worktree` (`image.rs:816`), the `close` parameter (`:827`, checks `:891-904`), `linked_worktree_evidence()` (`:972`), `CapturedAnswers.linked_worktree` (`:805`), `into_answers` (`:984,994`), `captured_byte_count` (`:1065,1083`).
- Types: `LinkedWorktreeSourceClass` (`image.rs:503-515`), `LinkedWorktreeEvidence` (`:517-584`), five `CaptureError` variants (`:1541-1550`), re-exported at `repository_state/mod.rs:60-61`.
- Gate evidence: `GateEvaluationEvidence.linked` (`commands/gate_check.rs:91-94`), filled at `:412-417,425`.
- Store: `repository_state_store.rs:597-601`, `:1218-1228`, `:1283-1307`, `capture_linked_evidence` at `:1580-1659`.
- 21 `RepositoryImage::close` call sites, one argument each. The investigation lists them.
- Prose: `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md:89`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CaptureSpec` has no linked-worktree entry, `RepositoryImage` and `CapturedAnswers` have no linked-worktree field, and `RepositoryImage::close` takes no linked-worktree argument.
- [hard] REQ-02: `LinkedWorktreeSourceClass`, `LinkedWorktreeEvidence`, the linked-evidence `CaptureError` variants and their re-exports no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: `GateEvaluationEvidence` has no linked-worktree field.
- [hard] REQ-04: Capturing a repository image never resolves worktree paths, and `capture_capability_image` takes no worktree-paths parameter.
- [hard] REQ-05: The repository-state materialization architecture note does not describe linked-worktree evidence.

## Notes

`configured_worktree_paths` stays for its other callers (`storage/json.rs:870,935`). `GitRevisionResolver::read_pinned_path` stays for `commands/archive.rs:99`. Tests of the removed evidence are deleted.

planning.outcome: Repository capture carries no linked-worktree evidence and spawns no git process for it.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Mechanical removal of one evidence chain, about 400 lines.

title: Remove inert configuration keys
description:
Four configuration surfaces are parsed and merged, yet no runtime command reads them: `worktree.mode` with `JIT_WORKTREE_MODE`, `[global_operations]`, `[locks]` and `[events]`. Only the configuration printers and checker reach them.

## Background

Declarations in `crates/jit/src/config.rs`:

- `JitConfig` fields `worktree` (`:54`), `global_operations` (`:58`), `locks` (`:60`), `events` (`:62`), and the config-absent literal (`:1510-1513`).
- `WorktreeModeError` (`:1188-1196`), `WorktreeConfig.mode` (`:1217`), `WorktreeMode` (`:1226-1262`), `WorktreeConfig::worktree_mode` (`:1308-1310`).
- `GlobalOperationsConfig` (`:1373-1391`), `LocksConfig` (`:1394-1410`), `EventsConfig` (`:1413-1429`), and their `Merged*` forms (`:2087-2172`).
- `EffectiveConfig::worktree_mode` (`:1749-1781`) and `global_operations()`/`locks()`/`events()` (`:1848-1882`).

They have three readers:

- `config show` (`main.rs:6804-6827`, `6834-6897`).
- `config get`, through `EffectiveConfig::full_snapshot` (`config.rs:1958-2001`, rustdoc `:1884-1912`).
- `config validate`, which checks `JIT_WORKTREE_MODE` (`main.rs:7006-7010`). Next to it, `main.rs:7016-7018` builds an effective config and discards it.

Other sites: the section list in `commands/config.rs:488`; `edit_config_document` type heuristics (`commands/config.rs:187-200`) whose bool branch matches only these keys; the rustdoc at `config_manager.rs:19`.

The `config validate` exit-4 failure lever is `env:JIT_WORKTREE_MODE=definitely-not-a-mode` (`tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml:129-136`, `command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs:510-522`). The `malformed-config-toml` setup kind already produces a post-dispatch invalid-config finding (`project_config_tests.rs:127-160`).

Documentation and adopter text that mention the keys: `docs/reference/configuration.md:29,582-590,651,667-670` (a "Parsed compatibility fields" section), `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3970-3979,4003-4005`, `docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md:257`, `docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:424`, the `profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml:440-466` comment block, `dev/eval/steering/README.md:58` and `dev/eval/steering/run_eval.py:69`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `JitConfig` declares no `worktree.mode`, `[global_operations]`, `[locks]` or `[events]`, and no code reads `JIT_WORKTREE_MODE`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `config show`, `config get` and `config validate` neither print nor check those keys or that variable.
- [hard] REQ-03: The configuration reference, the CLI reference, the how-to guides, the `jit-default` profile comment block and the steering evaluation do not mention them.
- [hard] REQ-04: The `config validate` exit-4 failure lever uses the `malformed-config-toml` setup kind, and the exit-code projection test passes with it.
- [hard] REQ-05: `edit_config_document`'s type heuristics hold no branch that matches only a key this change removes.

## Notes

Tests whose primary property is a removed key are deleted. Tests that mix removed and surviving keys keep the surviving assertions. `CHANGELOG.md:1027` is history and stays.

planning.outcome: The inert worktree-mode, operation, lock, and event settings are gone from code, tests, and docs.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One coherent key-family removal, about 800 deleted lines.

title: State each configuration default once
description:
Configuration defaults are written in several places: a per-layer accessor, a merged accessor, two printers and the prose. Each default gets one named statement that every reader derives from.

## Background

The defaults and where each is stated:

- `enforce_leases` (`Strict`): `crates/jit/src/config.rs:1317,1820,1966` and `main.rs:6807,6849`; prose at `docs/reference/configuration.md:482`. Which mode commands enforce, and how the value resolves across layers and the environment (including the no-section path at `config_manager.rs:111`), is owned elsewhere. This change moves where the default value is stated, not how it resolves.
- `[coordination]` timing keys: their declarations are being reduced elsewhere. Whichever of them still exist when this change lands are in scope like any other default.
- `max_indefinite_leases_per_agent = 2`: `config.rs:1364,2065`; prose at `configuration.md:560` and `profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml:453`.
- `max_indefinite_leases_per_repo = 10`: `config.rs:1368,2084`; prose at `configuration.md:564` and `manifest.toml:454`.
- `write_policy` is already one constant, `LinkedCheckoutWriteStance::DEFAULT`.

Only tests call the per-layer accessors (`config.rs:1335-1428`; tests at `:3508-3587`). Production uses the `Merged*` accessors (`config.rs:2009-2172`): `commands/claim.rs:112,143-144`, the printers, and `full_snapshot`. `config show` (`main.rs`) and `EffectiveConfig::full_snapshot` (`config.rs`) print the same merged view, each with its own `unwrap_or` defaults.

`crates/jit/src/runtime_defaults.rs` already projects named defaults into `docs/reference/runtime-defaults.md` (`scripts/generate-runtime-defaults-reference.sh`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each configuration default present when the change lands, including the `enforce_leases` default and any remaining `[coordination]` timing key, is stated once as one named constant, and no accessor, printer or prose restates its value.
- [hard] REQ-02: No per-layer default accessor remains, and the effective configuration reads each key's layers through one layered lookup over the repository, user and system layers.
- [hard] REQ-03: The resolution behaviour of `enforce_leases` across layers and the environment, and the mode commands enforce, are unchanged by this change.
- [hard] REQ-04: `config show` renders the same merged snapshot that `config get` returns.
- [hard] REQ-05: The runtime-defaults reference projects the lease-limit defaults, and the configuration reference and the `jit-default` profile comment cite it in place of the numbers.

## Notes

Configuration file I/O stays in `config.rs`; `main.rs` only renders. Each criterion holds in any order relative to the in-flight work on the `[coordination]` timing keys and on `enforce_leases` resolution. The criteria cover the keys that exist when this change lands, and the change neither adds nor removes keys.

planning.outcome: Each configuration default has one named statement that accessors, printers, and docs derive from.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One accessor-layer restructure over three defaults, about 200 lines net.

title: Reject unknown keys in config.toml
description:
`config.toml` loads silently when it holds a removed key or a typo, and the load error that does surface drops its cause. Loading becomes strict, and the error names the offending key.

## Background

No `config.toml` type carries `deny_unknown_fields` except `IconConfigToml` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:219`). The tolerant types include `JitConfig` (`:12`), `VersionConfig` (`:84`), `ProjectConfig` (`:97`), `HierarchyConfigToml` (`:205`), `ValidationConfig` (`:253`), `DocumentationConfig` (`:315`), `NamespaceConfig` (`:420`), `ItemKindConfig` (`:516`), `TomlSourceDescriptor` (`:760`, reached through the visitor at `:690-726`), `ProjectionConfig` (`:1034`), `WorktreeConfig` (`:1214`) and `CoordinationConfig` (`:1334`). No configuration type uses `flatten` or a tagged enum. All three layers deserialize `JitConfig` (`config.rs:1677-1692`), through two paths: `JitConfig::load` (`:1531`) and `declarations::parse_configuration` (`declarations/mod.rs:65-69`, also `storage/ruleset_store.rs:146`).

`test_load_config_with_removed_keys_still_parses` (`config.rs:2701-2742`) asserts that stale configuration loads. Prose claims tolerance at `config.rs:248-252,415-419,1525-1529,2694-2698`.

The load error drops its cause. `JitConfig::load` wraps the error with `.context(...)` (`config.rs:1531`), and `main.rs:6989,6999` format it with `{}`, so `config validate` prints only `repo config: Failed to parse config.toml`. The declarations path already prints the TOML cause. With `deny_unknown_fields`, toml 0.8 reports ``unknown field `x`, expected one of ...``.

`config set --global` writes the user file without parsing it again (`commands/config.rs:243-251`). The repository scope re-parses through `declarations_from_image` (`commands/config.rs:327`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every type deserialized from `config.toml` rejects unknown fields, at each configuration layer and through both parse paths.
- [hard] REQ-02: Loading a `config.toml` that holds an unknown key fails with an error naming the key, wherever the configuration is loaded, including `config show` and `config validate`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `config set` parses the edited document as configuration before writing it, at both repository and global scope, and refuses an edit that would not load.
- [hard] REQ-04: No test asserts that stale configuration loads, and no prose claims tolerance of unknown keys. One owning test proves that an unknown key is rejected by name.
- [hard] REQ-05: No serde field alias remains on configuration types.

## Notes

`#[serde(skip)]` fields (`templates`, `invariants`) become unknown keys, as intended. Inline test configuration strings that carry undeclared keys are corrected (`test_utils.rs`, `test_taxonomy.rs`, `repository_state/materialize.rs` tests compose configurations from strings). `CoordinationConfig` gets the attribute like every other configuration struct, whatever fields it holds when this change lands. This repository's `.jit/config.toml` uses only declared keys.

planning.outcome: config.toml loading rejects an unknown key with an error naming it, at each layer.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: About fifteen attributes, one error-cause fix, one post-edit parse.

title: Reject unknown keys in rule declarations
description:
Rule declarations accept unknown keys and two selector aliases. Three assertion kinds are untyped tables, so a misspelled key surfaces late as a configuration finding, or never.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/declarations/rules.rs`, `RawRulesFile` (`:879`), `RawRule` (`:886`) and `Selector` (`:223`) lack `deny_unknown_fields`; the `RawAssert` family (`:908-1116`) already has it. The selector accepts the aliases `has-doc-type` (`:237`) and `doc_type` (`:1110`), the only `serde(alias)` uses in configuration, agent and rule types. Both writers emit `has_doc_type` (`repository_state/rule_serialize.rs:210`, `commands/validate.rs:2953`), and so does `docs/reference/configuration.md:411`. `docs/how-to/validation-rules.md:87` documents the alias, and so does the rustdoc at `validation/graph.rs:1363`.

`label-coverage`, `label-reference` and `dependency-shape` are untyped `toml::value::Table`s (`rules.rs:923-927`), interpreted late in `validation/graph.rs`: label-coverage keys at `:860-935`, and dependency-shape `target`/`mode`/`transitive` at `:1380-1403`, where `target` becomes a `Selector` only at evaluation. They are serialized back verbatim (`rule_serialize.rs:267-275`). The `kind` sugar is expanded by `expand_kind_sugar` (`rules.rs:1403`). Two tests assert tolerance of unknown table keys: `test_label_coverage_inline_rule_unchanged_with_extra_unknown_key` (`rules.rs:2869`) and `test_label_coverage_inline_rule_with_stray_kind_key_is_inert` (`:2894`). `RawGateRecency` shows the typed raw-struct pattern.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `RawRulesFile`, `RawRule` and `Selector` reject unknown fields at load.
- [hard] REQ-02: `label-coverage`, `label-reference` and `dependency-shape` assertions are checked at load through typed raw structs that reject unknown keys. `dependency-shape` `target` parses as a selector at load, and the `kind` sugar is a typed optional field.
- [hard] REQ-03: The selector key is spelled only `has_doc_type`, and `has-doc-type` and `doc_type` are rejected.
- [hard] REQ-04: Loading a rule declaration with an unknown key fails with an error naming the key.
- [hard] REQ-05: The two tolerance tests assert rejection. `docs/how-to/validation-rules.md` and the `validation/graph.rs` rustdoc use `has_doc_type`.

## Notes

After the load-time check, the three assertion payloads keep their table representation. Full typing of the assertion model is a separate semantic-types refactor. This repository's `.jit/rules.toml` uses only declared keys.

planning.outcome: Rule declarations reject unknown keys at load and spell the doc-type selector one way.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three typed raw tables plus alias removal in one parser.

title: Keep one agent configuration type
description:
`agent.toml` has two Rust types that disagree on optionality, and the resolver its tests exercise is a test-only copy of the production function. One strict type remains, behind one resolver.

## Background

- Production type: `agent_config::AgentConfig`/`AgentSection` (`crates/jit/src/agent_config.rs:23-41`, `load()` at `:43-74`). `created_at` and `description` are required, and it tolerates a legacy `[behavior]` block (`:20-22`, test `:271-290`).
- Test-only type: `config::AgentConfig`/`AgentIdentity` (`config.rs:1434-1481`), with every field optional, used only by six tests (`config.rs:3637-3726`), including a `[behavior]` twin test at `:3659-3676`.
- `#[cfg(test)] fn resolve_agent_id_with_env` (`agent_config.rs:121-155`) duplicates `resolve_agent_id` (`:82-112`). Its tests (`:288-353`) call the real `AgentConfig::load()` (`:140`), which reads `dirs::config_dir()/jit/agent.toml`. `test_resolve_agent_id_no_config_error` (`:342`) therefore passes only on hosts without that file.
- `AgentSection.default_ttl_secs` (`agent_config.rs:39-40`) is never read. `docs/reference/configuration.md:621-623` calls it "parsed metadata only".

Production callers of `resolve_agent_id`: `commands/claim.rs:105,241,300,435,483`, `commands/template.rs:301`, `commands/mod.rs:728,753,3269`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `config::AgentConfig` and `config::AgentIdentity` no longer exist, and `agent_config::AgentConfig` is the only agent configuration type.
- [hard] REQ-02: The resolver function the tests call is the one production calls, with the environment lookup and the configuration loader as parameters. No `cfg(test)` copy remains.
- [hard] REQ-03: Resolver tests read no host configuration file or process environment variable.
- [hard] REQ-04: An `agent.toml` with an unknown key, including a `[behavior]` block, fails to load with an error naming the key.
- [hard] REQ-05: `default_ttl_secs` is not an agent configuration field, and the configuration reference does not document it.

## Notes

`created_at` and `description` stay required, as production has them. Tests for the removed type are deleted.

planning.outcome: One strict agent configuration type exists, and tests call the production agent-id resolver.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One type deleted, one resolver seam, about 170 lines.

title: Keep one profile manifest version
description:
Both shipped profiles still declare manifest version 1. The decoder accepts versions 1 and 2, and they hash package identity differently. Version 2 becomes the only wire version.

## Background

- `profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml:10` and `profiles/jit-dogfood/manifest.toml:4` declare `manifest-version = 1`. The dogfood manifest's `dependencies = ["jit-default"]` becomes a `[[dependency]]` table, which version 1 decoded as requirement `"*"` (`crates/jit/src/profile/wire.rs:84-90`).
- `docs/reference/profiles.md:93-99` says the decoder "continues to accept version-1 manifests".
- Version-1 decoding parses the TOML four times (`wire.rs:52`, `:72`, and twice at `:96` through `v1_declares_template_field`). It hashes canonical JSON of the wire (`:79`, through `canonicalize` at `:240-253`), while version 2 hashes the source bytes (`:156`). The error text is at `wire.rs:17,42-43`.
- Twelve files spell version 1: the two profiles; fixtures `crates/jit/tests/fixtures/profile-packages/{synthetic-valid,planner-asset-only,planner-invalid-interpolation}/manifest.toml`; inline strings in `profile/manifest.rs:422`, `profile/package.rs` (the version-1 literal and the `legacy_v1_identity_hash` oracle, `:1040-1114,1225-1243`), `profile/package_capture.rs:871`, `wire.rs` tests (`:261-300,370-420`), `commands/profile.rs`, `test_utils.rs`, `tests/cli_repo_workflow/{profile_cli_tests.rs,profile_edit_refresh_cli_tests.rs}`; and `scripts/release_version_contract_test.py:172`.
- `scripts/release-version-contract.py:466-468` reads the version-1 key `jit` from the dogfood manifest.
- `profile/package.rs:1465` pins the synthetic-valid package hash.
- The decoder-ownership authority test (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:1382`) checks `profile/wire.rs`.

Target hashes derive from canonical contributions and do not change. This repository records no applied-profile hash.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Both shipped profiles, every fixture and every inline test manifest declare `manifest-version = 2`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The decoder rejects every other version with an error naming the version, and it parses a manifest once.
- [hard] REQ-03: Package identity hashes the manifest source bytes. The version-1 types, the version-1 decoder, the template-field probe and the canonical-JSON identity function no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-04: `scripts/release-version-contract.py` reads `compatible-jit`, and its test fixture uses the version-2 form.
- [hard] REQ-05: `docs/reference/profiles.md` documents version 2 alone.
- [hard] REQ-06: The decoder-ownership authority test asserts the decoder's current ownership. Regenerating the template region and the project projections produces no diff, and repository validation passes here.

## Notes

The pinned synthetic-valid hash is re-derived or replaced by a relational assertion. The legacy-identity oracle test is deleted. If the identity change invalidates an applied-profile record in this repository, the dogfood profile is re-applied in the same change.

planning.outcome: Profile manifests have one wire version, version 2, with one identity hashing scheme.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One decoder simplification plus mechanical fixture conversion.

title: Remove the read-lock sidecar sweep
description:
Listing issues sweeps `.jit/issues/` once per process for retired read-lock sidecars. The sweep misses short-id sidecars, and a trait method exists only to keep it out of one caller.

## Background

- `list_issues` runs the sweep at `crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1304-1324`, guarded by `sidecars_swept` (`:395-397,442`), through the helper at `storage/lock.rs:440-492`. The helper requires `Uuid::parse_str(stem)` (`lock.rs:480-484`), so it skips short-id names. This repository holds 19 such files (`003f.lock`, `003f9f83.lock`, and others), untracked and ignored by `.gitignore:5`.
